# Results — Study 729 ("the ramen index" — instant-noodle sales as a downturn tell)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Does instant-noodle demand
**lead** a recession / an equity drawdown, and are the noodle makers a defensive hide-out? We
test the **ramen index** — WINA world-demand (hardcoded, cited, **approximate** — a labelled
proxy) — for the leading-indicator claim, and the two tradable noodle makers **Nissin Foods
Holdings (`2897.T`)** and **Toyo Suisan (`2875.T`)** against the **Nikkei 225 (`^N225`)** on
beta, recession-window returns and tradability. Prices are real (month-end Adj Close,
yfinance); the WINA series and NBER windows are **hardcoded, cited**. Offline & deterministic;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Noodle names | `2897.T` (Nissin Foods Holdings, Tokyo) · `2875.T` (Toyo Suisan / Maruchan, Tokyo) — month-end Adj Close via yfinance, cached under `_cache/` |
| Benchmark | `^N225` (Nikkei 225, month-end, yfinance) — the market the noodle stocks actually trade in |
| Adjustment | `auto_adjust=True` — splits **and** dividends folded in (*total-return-ish*; labelled as such, not price-only) |
| The "ramen index" | **WINA** world instant-noodle demand, billions of servings/yr, 2005–2024 — **hardcoded, cited, approximate** ([`docs/references.md`](references.md)); a labelled proxy, not a live feed |
| Recession windows | **NBER** contractions: 2001-03→2001-11, 2007-12→2009-06, 2020-02→2020-04 — **hardcoded, cited**; dated facts, not a feed |
| As-of | 2026-06-30 (month-end; no partial-month bar) |
| Window | noodle names 2001-01 → 2026-06 (305 monthly returns); `^N225` from 2000-01 (317) |

> **Survivorship, named on the Signal axis.** These are the two *surviving* Japanese
> noodle **champions**, hand-picked ex-post; the selection points **for** any outperformance,
> so the significant alpha below (§4) is treated as a survivorship + weak-benchmark artefact,
> **not** as evidence for the recession-tell claim, which is what this study actually tests.

## Half 1 — THE HEADLINE: does the ramen index *lead* the market?

Lead-lag cross-correlation of WINA demand **growth** (%/yr) against the Nikkei's **annual
return**, aligned by calendar year (n = 19). `lead = +k` means demand *precedes* the market by
k years; a real downturn tell needs a **negative** correlation at a **positive** lead, with
|*t*| ≥ 2.

| lead (yrs) | corr *r* | *t* | p | reading |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| −2 | −0.34 | −1.51 | 0.15 | (market leads demand, if anything) |
| −1 | +0.31 | +1.32 | 0.20 | |
| 0 | +0.12 | +0.51 | 0.62 | contemporaneous — near zero |
| **+1** | **−0.25** | **−1.05** | 0.31 | the "tell" lead — **not significant** |
| +2 | −0.03 | −0.12 | 0.91 | |

**No lead clears |*t*| ≥ 2.** The best "demand-leads-a-downturn" correlation (+1 year) is
*t* = **−1.05** — indistinguishable from noise on this sample. The ramen index does not lead.

And the direct "demand jumps in a downturn" contrast (mean growth in NBER recession years vs
all others):

| | mean demand growth | n years |
|---|--:|--:|
| recession years | +2.02%/yr | 4 |
| other years | +1.93%/yr | 15 |
| **difference** | **+0.09%/yr** (*t* = **+0.02**, p = 0.98) | |

Demand grows at essentially the **same** rate whether or not the economy is in recession. The
"noodle demand spikes when times are hard" premise is not in the global series: WINA demand
actually **fell** in the 2008 GFC (−4.2% in 2008, −3.8% in 2009) and also fell in **2014–2016
with no recession at all**. The only genuine spike is **2020 (+9.6%)** — a COVID
pantry-loading / lockdown supply story, not a business-cycle tell.

## Half 2 — full-sample risk/return (what "holding noodles" did)

| series | CAGR | ann. vol | Sharpe | max drawdown | $1 → |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **2897.T** (Nissin) | +6.14% | 20.2% | 0.40 | −42.7% | $4.54 |
| **2875.T** (Toyo Suisan) | **+11.53%** | 25.8% | **0.55** | −36.6% | **$16.02** |
| `^N225` (Nikkei) | +4.95% | 19.2% | 0.35 | −62.8% | $3.59 |

Both noodle names **beat** the Nikkei over ~25 years — but that is the low-beta staple /
survivorship story of §4, not the recession tell of §1.

## Half 3a — downside defensiveness (bull vs bear beta, split at `^N225` = 0)

| name | down-beta β⁻ | up-beta β⁺ | full beta | asymmetry (β⁻−β⁺) | defensive? |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--:|
| **2897.T** | 0.47 | −0.05 | 0.20 | **+0.52** | **no** |
| **2875.T** | 0.14 | 0.27 | 0.31 | −0.13 | yes (weakly) |

Same "two names disagree" signature as the sibling beer study: Nissin loads *more* on the
downside (β⁻ > β⁺), Toyo Suisan slightly *less*. Both full betas are **≈0.2–0.3** — these are
very low-beta stocks, which is not the same as counter-cyclical.

## Half 3b — recession-window returns vs the Nikkei

Paired monthly excess `r_stock − r_N225` over the union of NBER recession months (n = 31):

| name | mean monthly (stock) | vs N225 | excess | *t* | p | cum (stock vs N225) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **2897.T** | −0.60% | −2.15% | +1.55%/mo | **+0.94** | 0.352 | −25.0% vs −54.1% |
| **2875.T** | +1.37% | −2.15% | +3.53%/mo | **+1.34** | 0.189 | +17.0% vs −54.1% |

**Neither clears |*t*| ≥ 2.** Per-recession breakdown (compounded %):

| recession | n | 2897.T | 2875.T | `^N225` |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2001 dot-com | 9 | −7.5% | +6.9% | −17.0% |
| 2008 GFC | 19 | −24.6% | −3.1% | −36.5% |
| 2020 COVID | 3 | +7.6% | +13.0% | −13.0% |

Both names fell (or nearly so) in the two *equity* recessions (2001, 2008) — just less than a
collapsing Nikkei — and only "won" cleanly in 2020, the COVID window, which is exactly the
pantry-loading episode, not a repeatable recession edge.

## Half 4 — CAPM alpha vs the Nikkei (Newey-West, 6-lag) — the honest complication

| name | annualised α | beta | NW *t*(α) | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **2897.T** | +6.54% | 0.20 | **+2.03** | 0.044 |
| **2875.T** | +12.20% | 0.31 | **+2.79** | 0.006 |

These alphas **do** clear |*t*| ≥ 2 — but they are **not** the claim under test. Three reasons
they are not evidence for "the ramen index is a downturn tell":
1. **They are about *outperforming the Nikkei*, not about *leading recessions*.** §1 already
   showed the demand series carries no cycle information.
2. **Survivorship.** These are two hand-picked *surviving* noodle champions; the selection
   manufactures outperformance (a dead brewer would not be in the sample).
3. **Weak benchmark + low beta.** β ≈ 0.2–0.3 against the Nikkei — a market that returned
   ~5%/yr through Japan's lost decades. Beating *that* with a defensive staple is the low-vol /
   quality premium, freely available, not a ramen recession signal.

## Synthetic positive controls — the engines are faithful

- **Lead-lag control.** A deterministic index engineered to *genuinely lead* the market by
  **1 year** (seed 729): the cross-correlation engine recovers `best_lead = 1`, *r* ≈ **−0.93**,
  *t* ≈ **−15.1** — so the flat null on the real ramen tape (§1) is a *real* null, not a blind
  detector.
- **Defensive control.** A stock with a planted asymmetric beta (β⁻ = 0.50, β⁺ = 1.00, seed
  7290): the bull/bear engine recovers β⁻ ≈ **0.71 < β⁺ ≈ 0.98**, `recovered_defensive = 1`.

## Tradability — a *double* look-ahead kills the tell

The recession-tell strategy needs to know **both** (a) this year's global noodle demand — which
WINA publishes only **~6 months into the *next* year** — and (b) that a recession is coming —
which the NBER dates only **~12 months ex-post**. So "buy defense when the ramen index spikes"
is a look-ahead on both legs; you cannot act on the tell in real time. And the only thing that
*did* beat the market (the §4 alpha) is a survivorship-selected low-beta staple, not the tell.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** On the claim actually under test — the ramen index as a *leading
  downturn tell* — nothing clears the bar: the best lead correlation is *t* = **−1.05**,
  demand grows the same in and out of recessions (*t* = +0.02), and the recession-window
  excess is insignificant (*t* = +0.94 / +1.34). The significant item on the tape (§4 alpha vs
  the Nikkei) is a survivorship + weak-benchmark artefact, explicitly **not** the tell.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A double look-ahead (WINA ~6 mo late + NBER ~12 mo late) makes the
  tell un-implementable, and the "buy the noodle makers" version rests on picking the survivors
  ex-post.
- **A leading tell? — BUSTED.** The one comprehensive demand series shows the "recession spike"
  is a single COVID datapoint; demand *fell* in the 2008 GFC and fell again in 2014–2016 with no
  recession. Instant noodles are a secular Asian growth story, not a business-cycle instrument.

> **Caveat (named, not buried).** The macro sample is tiny (19 annual demand observations, 4
> recession years) so the lead-lag test is low-power by construction — but a low-power test that
> *also* points the wrong way (demand fell in the GFC) cannot certify a "ramen predicts
> recessions" law. A US-only instant-noodle sales series (the folklore's original anecdote) may
> behave differently from the global WINA figure used here; that is flagged, not hidden.
